title: A Protocol for the Border
premise: Marguerite Pemberton's firm, Coldharbour Protective Services, exists to make powerful people untraceable, and its crowning asset is a ledger of erased flights, identities, and debts. When a charter he personally cleared disappears from every database mid-flight and crashes off the coast with no survivors on record, Marguerite realizes someone inside his own found family of fixers sold the protocol. To survive the night and expose the buyer—a border authority official laundering influence through the very checkpoints his clients must cross—he must trade the ledger itself, the one secret worth killing for, before the checkpoint shifts change at dawn. He burns the archive, saves the traitor who once saved him, and walks through the border as a man with no records at all.
about_author: Coral Coldharbour is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting things that officially never happened. They write from a coastal town where the fog rolls in exactly on schedule.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. A routine erasure job unravels when charter KX-114 vanishes from radar logs while still airborne, then from existence entirely. Marguerite's protégé, Ines, insists it's a glitch; his gut says otherwise. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the first crack in the professional invisibility he's built his life around.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Marguerite and Ines. Digging into the crash, they find the flight was carrying a witness against Deputy Director Voss, whose checkpoint network launders the firm's own dirty contracts. Someone inside leaked the protocol. Suspicion poisons the team's loyalty; Marguerite hides that he's already been offered a trade—his ledger for his life. Beat: paranoia tightening into betrayal.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. Cornered at the border crossing as Voss's men close in, Marguerite discovers the traitor is Ines, coerced by threats to her family—but she's also fed him the evidence to destroy Voss. The climax erupts in the checkpoint's fluorescent corridors: a standoff over the ledger, guns and leverage, dawn approaching. Beat: loyalty and truth colliding head-on.

chapters.title: No Records
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite. Marguerite hands Voss a decoy drive, lets the real ledger burn, and releases proof of the crash to the press as the shift changes and the checkpoint opens. Ines walks free; the firm dissolves; Marguerite crosses the border as nobody, finally invisible by choice rather than trade. Beat: grief, release, and hard-won freedom.
